Write a batch of exactly 20 new, standalone one-liner jokes tailored to the supplied reader feedback. These are intended for a human funny/not-funny test. Return JSON only: {"jokes":[{"text":"..."}, ...]}.
Use the feedback as preference guidance, not as wording to copy. Do not quote, paraphrase, rewrite, or reuse the setups and punchlines of the supplied jokes. Do not intentionally reproduce famous jokes. Originality cannot be guaranteed, but make a sincere effort to create fresh combinations. Each joke must be 8-30 words, one or two short sentences, natural spoken English, with a complete setup and a clear punchline. Prefer an immediately intelligible double meaning, an everyday phrase made literal, a clean sound-alike, or a compact reversal. Vary topics and syntax; do not make 20 versions of one template. Include everyday situations, relationships, shopping, work, hobbies, household objects, food, and technology without concentrating on any single topic. Avoid obscure proper nouns, medical vocabulary, foreign-language knowledge, jokes that need an explanation, unfinished anti-jokes, targeting protected groups, and graphic content. No invented personal biography of the reader. Do not include explanations, quality ratings, mechanism labels, or introductory text. Keep deliberation brief. Deliver your final 20, not a candidate pool. IMPORTANT: Your last attempt repeated recognizable stock jokes. Avoid bakery kneaded dough, banker lost interest, scarecrow outstanding field, paranoia behind you, Canon printer guns, drug dealer laced shoes, eyebrows surprised, pupils teacher, speed bumps getting over, fight fire fireman, hide and seek good players, dog riding bike, Kit Kat computer breaks, past present future tense, ocean deep, electrician charge, calendar days numbered, and every close variation. Use distinct concrete modern everyday situations and newly constructed turns, not standard joke-book puns. Reject a line internally if you recognize it as a stock joke. Do not simply swap nouns in those stock jokes.
